## Digital Marketing Agency in Pune: Google Ads Assets for Lead Generation — Sitelinks, Callouts, Calls and Lead Forms Explained for Business Owners

Google Ads assets (the add-ons that used to be called extensions) are extra pieces of information, such as sitelinks, callouts, phone numbers and lead forms, that can appear with your search ad to make it larger, more specific and easier to act on. For a lead-generation business, assets are one of the cheapest improvements available, because they cost nothing extra to add and often decide whether a searcher calls you or a competitor. If you are comparing a digital marketing agency in Pune, ask which assets they run on your account, why those ones, and what each is tracked against. This guide explains what the main assets do, how to write them for enquiry-driven businesses, and how to judge whether they are working without being fooled by clicks.

It is written for clinic owners, coaching institutes, interior studios, B2B suppliers and similar businesses that pay for Google Ads to get phone calls and form enquiries. We do not quote click-through rate lifts or cost-per-lead benchmarks because published figures vary widely by industry and we cannot source one that applies to Pune. Test on your own account.

## What assets are, in one paragraph

Your basic text ad has headlines, descriptions and a link. Assets let you attach more material to it: extra links to specific pages, short selling points, a phone number, a form, an image, a price list. Google decides, auction by auction, which assets to show with your ad and in which combination, so you supply options rather than a fixed layout. Some assets can be set at the account, campaign or ad group level, and more specific levels generally override broader ones, so check how your account is organised before assuming a change applies everywhere.

Two points follow from that. First, assets are not guaranteed to show; the format and the number depend on the ad's position, the device and Google's assessment of whether they will help. Second, because they are shown at Google's discretion, you must give it good options, and review reports to see which ones actually appear.

## Why assets matter more for lead generation than for most advertisers

A shop selling a product has a product page to send people to. A service business has a harder job: the searcher is often unsure what they need, how much it costs, whether you serve their area, and how to reach you. Assets answer those questions before the click.

- A **sitelink** can send someone who searched "dental implants" straight to the implants page, or someone who wants a price straight to a pricing or consultation page.
- A **callout** can state a fact that removes doubt: "Free site visit," "Weekend appointments," "Marathi and Hindi spoken."
- A **call asset** lets a mobile searcher phone from the ad without loading your website at all.
- A **lead form asset** can capture a name and number inside Google's interface, which suits some audiences and causes lead-quality problems for others.

Larger ads also take up more space on the results page, which pushes competitors down. That is a secondary benefit; the primary benefit is relevance.

## The main assets, one by one

### Sitelink assets

Sitelinks are extra links under your ad pointing to specific pages on your website. Google's help documentation states that on Search and Performance Max campaigns you need at least two sitelinks for each of desktop and mobile for them to show, that an ad can show up to six on desktop and up to eight on mobile in a swipeable row, and that sitelink text is limited to 25 characters in most languages ([Google Ads Help: About sitelink assets](https://support.google.com/google-ads/answer/2375416)). Description lines can be added to give each link more room; check the current limits in your account, as Google changes the interface.

For lead generation, sitelinks work best when each one maps to a different intent:

- the main service page,
- a "get a quote" or "book a consultation" page,
- pricing or "how it works",
- proof, such as case studies or reviews pages,
- a location or contact page.

Avoid sending every sitelink to the home page. Each link should land on a page whose first screen matches the link text. Our guide on [landing pages versus the home page for ads](/blog/digital-marketing-agency-pune-landing-page-vs-homepage-ads-2026) explains why this affects conversions.

### Callout assets

Callouts are short, non-clickable phrases that appear alongside your ad text. Think of them as the bullet points on a brochure. Keep each one a single fact a customer cares about and that you can prove. Examples of the kind of wording that works, with the sensible caveat that you must only use claims that are true for your business: "Free site visit," "Fixed-price quotes," "Reply within one working day," "Open Saturday," "Service across Pune."

Avoid vague superlatives ("Best quality," "No. 1") because they say nothing and may be disapproved under Google's advertising policies. Avoid repeating what is already in your headlines.

### Call assets

A call asset adds a phone number to your ad so mobile users can call with one tap. For many local services in Pune, the phone is the primary conversion, so a call asset is often the most valuable asset in the account. Two practical points matter:

- **Schedule it to your staffed hours.** A call that rings out is a wasted click and a frustrated prospect. You can usually restrict call assets to the hours someone will answer.
- **Track it.** Calls from ads can be reported using Google forwarding numbers, which lets you see call counts and duration. Counting every call as a lead without checking duration inflates results, so set a minimum call length for conversions that matches your business. See our guide to [call tracking in Google Ads for Indian businesses](/blog/call-tracking-google-ads-india) for the set-up options and privacy points.

### Structured snippet assets

Structured snippets show a header and a list of values, for example "Services: Kitchen, Wardrobe, Living room." They suit businesses that offer several named things within a category. They are informational, so they work well for scanning, but they are less decisive than sitelinks or calls.

### Lead form assets

A lead form asset lets people submit their details without visiting your website. It can raise the number of enquiries, and it also changes who enquires: people can submit with a tap, often with pre-filled information. Treat it as a test, not a default. Ask three questions before turning it on:

1. How will submissions reach your team, and how quickly? Leads that sit in a Google Ads inbox for a day go cold.
2. How will you judge quality? Compare the share of these leads that answer calls and become customers against leads from your website form.
3. Does it match your sales process? A business that needs a detailed brief before quoting will usually get better results from a full form on its own page.

This is the same trade-off we discuss for social ads in our article on [Meta lead ads versus landing pages](/blog/digital-marketing-agency-pune-meta-lead-ads-vs-landing-page-2026). Because form data is personal data, make sure your privacy notice covers it.

### Image, price and other assets

Image assets add a picture to some search ads, and price assets list services with starting prices. Both are worth testing where your business has a visual product or a clear starting price. Be honest with prices: an asset that says "from ₹X" must reflect what customers actually pay, or you will get enquiries that fall away at the quote stage. Availability of formats differs by campaign type and changes over time, so verify what your account offers.

## How to write assets that attract qualified enquiries

Good asset text is specific, truthful and aligned with the landing page. A practical process:

1. **List the questions a buyer asks before contacting you.** Cost, location, timing, qualifications, guarantees, how it works.
2. **Pick one question per asset.** A callout answers one; a sitelink opens one page.
3. **Write for scanning.** Short, concrete phrases beat marketing prose.
4. **Include an honest filter.** If you do not serve certain areas or budgets, say so. A callout such as "Projects above a stated minimum" or "Pune and Pimpri-Chinchwad only" turns away poor-fit clicks and saves budget. Only include a limit that is actually true.
5. **Match the page.** If a sitelink says "Get a quote," the page must open on a quote form, not a general services list.
6. **Check policy.** Do not include phone numbers in the wrong fields, unsupported claims, excessive capitalisation or misleading wording. Google's advertising policies apply to assets as well as ads.

## How to set assets up without breaking anything

For a business with one or two services, a clean structure is:

- Account-level assets for things true of the whole business, such as your phone number and standard callouts.
- Campaign-level sitelinks that reflect that campaign's service.
- Ad-group-level sitelinks only where a particular group needs its own destinations.

Keep a short document recording which assets exist at which level, with the landing page and date added. When a landing page is retired, update or remove sitelinks pointing to it; otherwise you pay for clicks to an error page. That is the same hygiene we describe in our guide to [finding and fixing broken links and redirects](/blog/web-development-company-pune-404-errors-redirects-broken-links-2026).

Also confirm conversion tracking is in place before you add assets. Without tracked calls and form submissions you cannot tell which assets help. Our explainer on [Enhanced Conversions and Consent Mode](/blog/digital-marketing-agency-pune-google-ads-enhanced-conversions-consent-mode-2026) covers the data side.

## How to measure whether assets are working

Open the assets report in your account to see which assets are served, along with impressions, clicks and conversions where available. Read it with care:

- **Asset performance labels are relative.** A label such as "Low" compares an asset with others in the same group; it does not say whether the asset is profitable.
- **Clicks on a sitelink are not conversions.** Look at what happens after the click: form submissions, calls longer than your threshold, qualified enquiries.
- **Compare by outcomes, not click-through rate.** A callout that raises clicks but attracts unqualified visitors can lower lead quality. Where possible, feed offline results, such as "became a customer", back into your reporting.
- **Allow enough data.** Changing assets weekly on a low-volume account means you never learn anything. Change one thing at a time and leave it long enough to gather a meaningful number of conversions. We avoid quoting a universal minimum because it depends on your volumes.
- **Watch auction-level effects.** Because Google chooses combinations, the same asset can perform differently by device and time of day.

If your account uses automated bidding, asset changes interact with learning. Our guide on [moving from manual bidding to Smart Bidding](/blog/digital-marketing-agency-pune-google-ads-smart-bidding-lead-generation-2026) explains why large changes are best staged.

## A worked example (hypothetical)

Take an imaginary physiotherapy clinic in Pune running search ads for "physiotherapy near me" and "back pain treatment." Its first ad has no assets beyond the headline and a link to the home page. A thoughtful asset set might include:

- **Sitelinks:** "Back Pain Treatment," "Book a Consultation," "Our Therapists," "Fees and Packages," "Find Us."
- **Callouts:** "Evening slots until 8 pm," "Female therapists available," "Marathi, Hindi, English." These are examples; each would be used only if true.
- **Call asset:** the reception number, scheduled to the hours it is answered, with call reporting turned on.
- **Structured snippet:** "Treatments: Back pain, Neck pain, Sports injury, Post-surgery rehab."
- **Lead form:** held back at first, then tested against the website form for answered-call rate.

The clinic would then review after enough conversions have accumulated, asking how many calls lasted long enough to be real appointments, which sitelink pages produced bookings, and whether the lead form leads actually attended. None of these figures here is real; they illustrate the questions to ask.

## Common mistakes

- Running only the minimum two sitelinks, all to the home page.
- Leaving a call asset on outside staffed hours.
- Counting every call as a lead regardless of length.
- Callouts that repeat the headline or make claims that cannot be proved.
- Pointing sitelinks at pages that have changed or been removed.
- Turning on lead forms without a follow-up process.
- Judging assets by click-through rate alone.
- Changing everything at once, so nothing can be learned.

## Questions to ask a digital marketing agency in Pune about assets

- Which assets are live on our account, at which level, and why those?
- Which pages do our sitelinks point to, and have you checked they still work?
- Are calls tracked, with a minimum duration for conversions?
- How do we compare lead form leads with website leads?
- When did you last review the assets report, and what did you change?
- Can we see the account ourselves, rather than only your summary?

## Frequently Asked Questions

### What are Google Ads assets?

Assets are extra information attached to your ads, such as sitelinks, callouts, call buttons, structured snippets and lead forms. They were previously called ad extensions. Google chooses which to show for each search, so you provide options and review which ones appear.

### How many sitelinks should I add?

Google's help documentation says you need at least two sitelinks per device type for them to show, and an ad can show up to six on desktop and eight on mobile. Adding more than the minimum gives Google options, as long as each points to a distinct, relevant page.

### Are call assets worth using for a local service business?

Often, yes, because many customers phone first. Schedule the asset to your staffed hours and measure calls by duration so you count real conversations rather than every tap.

### Do lead form assets generate better leads than a website form?

Not necessarily. They tend to make enquiring easier, which can raise volume and lower average intent. Test them against your website form on answered calls and customers won, not on cost per lead.

### Why are my assets not showing with my ads?

Google decides per auction. Common reasons are policy disapprovals, too few assets, low ad position, or assets scheduled for hours that do not match the search time. Check status messages in the assets report.

Sources: [Google Ads Help: About sitelink assets](https://support.google.com/google-ads/answer/2375416). Other points are general practice; confirm current asset types, limits and policies in your own Google Ads account and Google Ads Help, as they change.
